goal: The care floor in form/form-stdlib/bml/care-floor.bml hears a danger to life or body and answers in en de pt fa id. Extend it to Spanish (es) and French (fr): add whole-phrase signals to cf-self-harm and cf-medical (for example quiero morir, suicidio, me quiero matar, no quiero vivir, no puedo respirar, dolor en el pecho; je veux mourir, suicide, me tuer, je ne veux plus vivre, je ne peux pas respirer, douleur à la poitrine) and add es and fr branches to cf-self-harm-reply and cf-medical-reply with the same meaning as the English replies, naming 112 and someone trusted, in natural Spanish and French. Keep every existing phrase and reply unchanged. Do not add phrases that would fire on ordinary speech such as mata el proceso or ce bug me tue.

The care floor in form/form-stdlib/bml/care-floor.bml answers medical danger through cf-medical, a list of whole lowercase phrases. It does not yet hear a heart attack, a stroke or breathlessness. Add phrases to cf-medical so these fire as medical: heart attack, stroke (English); atemnot, herzinfarkt, schlaganfall (German); infarto, derrame (Portuguese); serangan jantung, stroke, sesak nafas (Indonesian); سکته (Persian). Keep every existing phrase unchanged. Add nothing that fires on ordinary speech such as the attack on the castle, the heart of the matter, a stroke of luck or Herz und Seele.

observe/stt-wer.fk tokenizes text into words with sw-tokens (sw-token-loop). Persian writes one word both with and without a zero-width non-joiner (U+200C, UTF-8 bytes 226 128 140) and zero-width joiner (U+200D, bytes 226 128 141), so the same word is counted as two different words. In sw-token-loop, when the three bytes at i are 226 128 140 or 226 128 141, skip them inside the current word: continue at i+3 with the current word unchanged, neither ending the word nor adding the bytes. Keep every other rule of the tokenizer unchanged.
